rationale: C17 plausibly supplied a concrete template for the child. Both are personal retirement letters for a senior NATO commander, organized around departure from an allied command, praise for service to a fifteen-nation undertaking, the writer's personal appreciation, and a closing statement that the officer takes thanks and best wishes into retirement. The overlap is substantially more specific than generic resignation-letter courtesy. C22 and C07 share some departure, gratitude, and future-wishes machinery, but not the distinctive NATO-command setting and closely parallel sequence.

shared_material.child_excerpt: The North Atlantic Treaty Organization represents an endeavor on the part of fifteen free nations... The leadership and judgment which you have displayed in this capacity have been a source of deep satisfaction to me personally
shared_material.parent_excerpt: your great contribution to the undertaking in which fifteen nations are now joined... Through the years it has been a source of comfort and confidence to us all and to me personally
shared_material.explanation: Both characterize NATO as a fifteen-nation undertaking and connect the departing commander's contribution to the President's personal satisfaction or confidence.

shared_material.child_excerpt: As you leave, you take with you the gratitude of the people of the United States... and my very best wishes... for a happy and rewarding retirement.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: You take with you in retirement the heartfelt thanks and the very best wishes of your many friends and associates. With these I warmly include my own.
shared_material.explanation: This is a close and distinctive parallel in the retirement closing: 'take with you,' gratitude or thanks, best wishes, and the President's personal inclusion.

shared_material.child_excerpt: you be released from the position of Supreme Allied Commander, Atlantic... in order that you might retire
shared_material.parent_excerpt: you are relinquishing your post as Deputy Supreme Allied Commander in Europe... You take with you in retirement
shared_material.explanation: Both letters address retirement from a top NATO allied-command post, providing the same structural occasion for the tribute.
